newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty may test downside before rebound vs basket.
newsitem.headline: Zloty may test downside before rebound vs basket.

text.p: The Polish zloty eased some 0.3 point against the parity rate in early trade as local traders joined a currency buying trend sparked by a single large zloty sale just after opening, dealers said.

They expected the zloty may ease further if the dollar makes the expected gains against the mark on world markets during the day. They saw the zloty at around minus 1.5 to 1.7 from parity at day's low point, but said it would close firmer.
"The zloty may fall below minus 1.5 percent from parity, but should not stay there for long," said Andrzej Fiderkiewicz, forex dealer at Societe Generale.

At 0830 the zloty was at 1.24/1.30 weaker than the parity rate against minus 0.99/1.13 percent at opening. It was at 3.4930/50 to the dollar and 1.9010/20 to the mark against opening's 3.4800/900 and 1.8965/95 respectively.
On the money market one-day rates stabilised after the early easing with overnight rates at 21.50/21.90 percent against opening's 21.50/21.75.

Tomorrow/next rates were at 21.00/22.30 against 21.60/21.95 percent at opening. Dealers expect the National Bank of Poland to stage a reverse repo and an NBP-bill sale to drain the cash-heavy market and underpin falling rates.
Dealers said the cash surplus on the money market was due to the small scale of NBP drainages over the last several days.
